methods.label: Relate real roots to intersection points
methods.explanation: Each real root gives a value of the coordinate remaining after substitution, and the line equation uniquely determines the other coordinate. Thus each root gives one intersection point, distinct roots give distinct points, and every intersection point must arise this way. Therefore, there are \(2\) intersection points, choice A.
methods.levelReason: Uses only the meaning of an equation's solution and the coordinate correspondence produced by substitution.
